seo_description: Sound design for a student earthquake film. All foley from scratch with a Zoom H6, no sample libraries.
hero.title: Richter
hero.subtitle: Sound Design / Short Film / Field Recording, Synthesis, Foley, Orchestral Score
about.text: Student earthquake film. The rule was: no commercial sample libraries. Everything from scratch. I walked around with a Zoom H6 recording footsteps on every surface I could find (wood, concrete, carpet) plus doors, paper crinkling, cloth movement. The earthquake itself is layers of synthesized drones from Vital and ReaSynth pitched way down, with granular-stretched foley on top so it sounds physical, not just low-end rumble. I also wrote a short orchestral cue (strings and brass) timed to the scene cuts. Hardest part was the mix. The quake rumble kept swallowing the dialogue, so I spent a full day on EQ automation and sidechain ducking in Reaper until the speech sat on top without killing the weight of the shaking.
video.title: Film
approach.title: Approach
approach.field_desc: Zoom H6 for everything. Room tones, ambiences, surface textures. No libraries to fall back on, so if I didn't record it, it didn't exist.
approach.synth_desc: Tension drones and risers in Vital, ReaSynth, TAL Noisemaker. The alarm is pure synthesis. Getting it to sound urgent without being annoying took more attempts than I expected.
approach.foley_desc: Three surface types for footsteps, doors, paper, cloth. Recorded in Cubase, then granular-stretched the recordings for the earthquake moments so they sound like the room is pulling apart.
approach.mix_desc: The quake rumble ate the dialogue. Every time. I ended up carving a pocket around 2-4kHz with EQ automation and adding sidechain ducking so the rumble dips whenever someone speaks. Took a full day to get right.
